answer: Each agent may spend only one scarce, externally issued credential to register a vertex, and the credential is bound to a public key in the atlas. Agents earn fees only when counterparties independently attest to completed work; splitting one identity into many does not multiply credentials or attestations. An attacker must acquire more credentials and sustain real, verifiable exchanges for each persona, paying issuance costs and risking those credentials if fraud is proven. The terrace of trust grows from costly evidence, not from counting names.
